title: GDScript editor: Incorrect highlighting in certain cases (single-line for loops, multi-line func declarations)
body: ### Tested versions Versions i had on hand for testing: 3.5.1, 3.6, 4.1.2, 4.2.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.4.1, 4.5.0, 4.5.1. Wrong color within multiline func declaration: - Reproduced in all versions i tested. Wrong color in single-line for loop: - Reproduced in 4.3 and higher. - Not reproduced in 4.2.2 and lower. ### System information Windows 10 (build 19045) - Not tested on other platforms but no reason on earth to expect any difference ### Issue description There are a couple of cases where Godot's script editor gets the highlighting wrong. Namely the cases mentioned in the issue's title. In the case of a single-line for loop, it's that assigning a variable after the colon will color it "Base Type Color" green. It seems as if the highlighter wrongly thinks that it's a type as in the strong-typing pattern `var something: String = "hello"`. In the case of multi-line function declarations (that is, when within the parentheses to put each parameter on its own line), instead of being "Base Type Color" green like they are within a single-line declaration, type hints of inner classes take on the "Member Variable" blue. Built-in types and classes such as any derived from `Object` or `Node` are not affected by this. Custom script classes defined with `class_name` have the "User Type" color as expected. Not sure exactly what is happening there besides the highlighter possibly just not realizing it's within a function declaration. Naturally the fixes would be within [modules/gdscript/editor/gdscript_highlighter.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/36b92128b1bce1f98687add98c84fd70ae9b20ca/modules/gdscript/editor/gdscript_highlighter.cpp), but when i spent a few minutes on Sunday looking at the file i didn't really nail down where those fixes would have to take place. Lot going on in there. ### Steps to reproduce Open `script.gd` within the MRP in the Godot editor. Or open a blank project, create a new script and type or paste into it: ```gdscript class InnerClass: var data: Array[int] func foo( bar: InnerClass ): var data := bar.data for baz in data1: baz = baz + 3 ``` (Yes, i realize this code doesn't do what whoever would've written it apparently intended. Just the case to show the syntax highlighting in minimal lines.) Observe the highlighting: The parameter typing `InnerClass` should be green, and `baz` in line 8 should not. Note the putting of `bar.data` into a local variable, as when using `bar.data` directly to initiate the for loop the highlighting is as expected. The green `baz` could be anything, not just the loop variable, but it is in this case to keep the lines down. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [bad-hl-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22936127/bad-hl-mrp.zip)
